correctness.rationale: Under the stated one-dimensional objective and \(D>d_0\sqrt8\), all gradients entering the cutoff computations equal \(-G\). For dual-averaging D-Adaptation, assuming the estimate has not yet moved gives \(s_n=-nd_0G\), \(\gamma_n=(G\sqrt n)^{-1}\), and the published proposal reduces to \(R_n=(n^{3/2}-1-\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}i^{-1/2})/(2n)\). Exact radical enclosures give \(R_1,\ldots,R_7<1<R_8\). For dual-averaging Prodigy with \(\lambda_k=d_k^2\), the analogous proposal is \(P_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}i/\sqrt{i+1}\), with \(P_1,\ldots,P_4<1<P_5\). The assigned verifier replays the published recurrences and certifies the cutoff signs with rational square-root bounds.
residual_risks: The cutoffs concern the dual-averaging variants and only the first increase of the distance estimate.

value.rationale: Startup adaptation is the central advertised distinction between these learning-rate-free methods. The constant-subgradient objective isolates the estimator dynamics without confounding curvature or noise, and exact first-growth cutoffs are a meaningful finite boundary rather than an arbitrary iteration census. The eight-versus-five comparison gives a reproducible structural benchmark for the claimed acceleration.
residual_risks: The result does not establish that Prodigy has a uniformly better optimization transient after activation.
